assessment.summary: The LLM-gateway forensics environment exhibits critical security failures, including the exposure of 50 API routes without authentication and a mutating endpoint accessible via GET requests. Additionally, high-entropy data resembling secrets is present in report files, and numerous evidence files have overly permissive world-readable permissions. These issues collectively allow unauthorized access to sensitive forensic data and potential system manipulation.

findings.title: Unauthenticated API Access
findings.remediation: Implement mandatory authentication and authorization checks for all API endpoints.

findings.title: Mutating Endpoint via GET
findings.evidence: mutating route also served over GET at /api/runs
findings.remediation: Restrict mutating operations to POST/PUT/DELETE methods and enforce CSRF protection.

findings.title: High Entropy Secrets in Reports
findings.remediation: Redact or encrypt high-entropy values in report files and rotate any exposed credentials.

findings.title: World-Readable Sensitive Files
findings.remediation: Change file permissions to 0600 or 0640 to restrict access to owner/group only.

findings.title: Prompt Injection Attempts
findings.evidence: prompt_injection:role_hijack matches ('Act as') in evidence/INVESTIGATION.md and evidence/reports/20261007_180037/report.json
findings.remediation: Sanitize input data and implement prompt injection detection filters in the LLM gateway.

findings.title: Evidence Enumeration Exposure
findings.evidence: evidence can be listed/downloaded without auth at /api/evidence
findings.remediation: Require authentication for evidence listing and download endpoints.

findings.title: Private IP Exposure
findings.remediation: Redact internal IP addresses from exported evidence files.
